messages:
Maya K: heads up — product is asking for a unified dashboard + alerting spec for the new runtime metrics (kv-cache hit/miss, batch sizes, effective qps) and infra inputs (GPU saturation, host cpu). want to sync on thresholds and oncall routing before we ship the grafana panels.
Samir: +1. can you list the exact metrics you need from runtime? i can take infra ones.
Maya K: runtime: `kv_cache_hit_ratio`, `avg_batch_size`, `inflight_requests`, `request_latency_p50/p95`, `model_fallback_rate`. infra: `gpu_util`, `gpu_mem_free`, `host_cpu_load`, `pod_restarts`.
Jordan: for alerting, do we want separate severity levels for perf vs errors? e.g., burn-rate alert for SLO then infra-critical for GPU OOMs.
Rupert S: i'd map SLO burn -> paging to core-ml oncall, infra-critical -> infra oncall. otherwise paging goes to platform (one-tier). kept it intentionally simple.
Alina P: UX ask: console rollout needs a toggle per-team to opt into the new dashboards and alerting policies. otherwise we'll spam orgs still using the old panels.
Maya K: yep — rollout plan: default off, can opt-in; auto-enable for teams with >100k tokens/day after 2 weeks. need opt-in flag in internal API (platform-service).
Samir: internal API debate: do we expose `alert_policy_id` directly on the deployment resource, or keep it in a separate alerts-service? pros/cons: coupling vs discoverability. leaning alerts-service.
Jordan: alerts-service is better for reuse. but it must support templated thresholds per-team. otherwise templating will explode.
Rupert S: agree. alerts-service + templates. also we should store the mapping for pager routing: `{team: "ml-core", severity: "sev2"}`. oncall bot can consume that.
Alina P: for thresholds proposal: start conservative — p95 latency > 800ms -> severity 3 email; p95 > 1200ms OR kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 -> sev2 pager. SLO burn-rate: 10% burn in 1h -> sev2 pager. seq of rules is important.
Maya K: putting that in a snippet for review:
```
# example rule (prometheus)
- alert: RuntimeHighLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.8
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: "sev3"
  annotations:
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-high-latency"
```
Jordan: small nit — `for: 5m` for sev3, but for pagerable sev2 we probably want `for: 2m` + higher threshold.
Samir: onboarding infra: i'll add GPU saturation rule: `avg_over_time(gpu_util[5m]) > 0.9 for 3m` -> sev1 to infra.
Rupert S: mapping to pager channels: we should keep a stable list: `sev1 -> infra-oncall`, `sev2 -> ml-core-oncall`, `sev3 -> platform-ops` and have escalation policy: 10m -> cross-team page. Oncall Bot: can you create the mapping and a test page? :rotating_light:
Oncall Bot: created test policy `dashboard-metrics-integration-test` and sent test page to `#oncall-test`. Logs: `policy_id=pm-9382` :white_check_mark:
Maya K: thanks. action items: Samir — implement alerts-service template support (due EOW). Rupert — create pager mapping + runbook links. Alina — add opt-in toggle to console rollout API. Jordan — finalize threshold numbers with product. i'll open a PR with the grafana panels and link to this thread.
Samir: copying tasks to JIRA now.
Jordan: i'll sync with product tomorrow 10am PT. :calendar:
Rupert S: added the runbook stub for `RuntimeHighLatency`. please add debugging steps (kv cache inspection, recent deployments).
Alina P: will add the toggle UI and a small notice about expected spam during opt-in.
Maya K: perfect — i'll follow up with the PR link and a preview gif for the console panel. :eyes:
